The terminal-only fertility equation F=lambda^(n-1)(lambda-t)/P1 increases strictly, so crossing existence, uniqueness and ordering follow; conditions P_j>1-t are necessary and sufficient for growing-regime crossings. originality.rationale: The most directly related 2009 primary paper reports empirical nonincrease of first-to-penultimate absolute fertility sensitivities (S2), but does not give a terminal-stage iff criterion or a complete growth-driven n-rank staircase. A 2021 primary paper proves stronger flow identities about elasticities, which are scaled by entries and are not equivalent to an absolute fertility sensitivity ranking; a 2022 age-within-stage sensitivity analysis allows reversals without the present exact terminal thresholds. Targeted indexed mathematical searches and accessible preceding claims disclose no dominating theorem of this precise scope. This is a best-knowledge comparison, not proof of historical uniqueness; generic eigenvector formulas may permit retrospective derivation.

value.rationale: The condition P1>1-t is a sharp interpretable separation between life histories where long terminal survival can make the oldest stage the most sensitive to absolute fertility improvements despite population growth, and those where it cannot. The one-parameter family exhibits an exactly ordered sequence through every possible sensitivity rank, with precise critical demographic rates. This finishes a motivated classification left open by the 2009 simulated S2 ordering; not a random parameter slice, and practical limits are specified.
